subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How long is the Edexcel GCSE English Literature Paper 1 examination?
questions.explain: Paper 1 (Shakespeare and Post-1914 Literature) is a written exam lasting 1 hour 45 minutes.

questions.q: What proportion of the total GCSE qualification does Paper 1 contribute?
questions.explain: Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry 50% of the total GCSE marks.

questions.q: How many marks is Paper 1 worth in total?
questions.explain: Paper 1 is marked out of 80, split across the Shakespeare and Post-1914 sections.

questions.q: How are the set texts made available to students during the Paper 1 exam?
options: Closed book — no copies of the texts are allowed
Open book with students' own annotations permitted
Open book with clean copies of the whole texts
Full copies of both texts are provided in the paper
questions.explain: Paper 1 is a closed-book exam; only a short printed extract is given for the Shakespeare question.

questions.q: What are the two sections of Paper 1?
options: Section A: Shakespeare; Section B: Post-1914 British play or novel
Section A: 19th-century novel; Section B: Poetry
Section A: Poetry anthology; Section B: Unseen poetry
Section A: Modern prose; Section B: Unseen fiction
questions.explain: Section A tests one Shakespeare play and Section B tests one post-1914 British play or novel.

questions.q: Which assessment objective is NOT assessed anywhere in Paper 1?
questions.explain: On Edexcel, context (AO3) is assessed only in Paper 2, not in Paper 1.

questions.q: In this qualification, AO4 rewards a student's ability to:
options: use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures with accurate spelling and punctuation
analyse a writer's use of imagery and symbolism
explain the historical context of a text
compare the ideas in two different texts
questions.explain: AO4 assesses technical accuracy (SPaG) and is credited in the Shakespeare section of Paper 1.

questions.q: The extract-based part of the Shakespeare question mainly rewards a student's:
options: analysis of language, form and structure (AO2)
discussion of historical and social context (AO3)
questions.explain: The extract task focuses on close analysis of how the writer uses language, form and structure (AO2).

questions.q: On how many Shakespeare plays does a student write in Section A?
questions.explain: Students study and are examined on a single Shakespeare play from the set list.

questions.q: Which of the following is a set Shakespeare text on the Edexcel specification?
questions.explain: Macbeth is on the Edexcel set list, while Hamlet, King Lear and Othello are not.

questions.q: A soliloquy is best described as:
options: a speech in which a character alone on stage voices their inner thoughts
a quick exchange of dialogue between two characters
a stage direction describing a character's movement
the rhyming couplet that closes a scene
questions.explain: A soliloquy lets an isolated character reveal their private thoughts directly to the audience.

questions.q: The line 'A pair of star-cross'd lovers take their life' comes from which set play?
questions.explain: This line is from the Prologue of Romeo and Juliet, foreshadowing the lovers' fate.

questions.q: In Macbeth, the Witches' line 'Fair is foul, and foul is fair' is best identified as an example of:
questions.explain: The apparently contradictory statement is a paradox, signalling the play's inverted moral order.

questions.q: Who wrote the post-1914 play 'An Inspector Calls'?
questions.explain: An Inspector Calls was written by J.B. Priestley and first performed in 1945.

questions.q: Who wrote the novel 'Animal Farm'?
questions.explain: Animal Farm (1945) was written by George Orwell as a political allegory.

questions.q: The Section B text must be a post-1914 BRITISH play or novel. Which text would therefore NOT be eligible?
options: Of Mice and Men (an American novella)
questions.explain: Of Mice and Men is American, so it does not meet the 'British' requirement of this section.

questions.q: 'Animal Farm' is most widely read as an allegory of:
options: the Russian Revolution and its aftermath
questions.explain: Orwell's fable satirises the Russian Revolution and the rise of Stalinism.

questions.q: 'An Inspector Calls' is set in 1912 but was written in 1945; this time gap chiefly enables Priestley to use:
questions.explain: The audience knows of events after 1912 (such as the World Wars), so Birling's confident claims become dramatically ironic.

questions.q: A student quotes 'All animals are equal, but some are more equal than others' to show how power corrupts. This line is from:
questions.explain: The pigs' revised commandment in Animal Farm exposes how the ruling elite betray equality.

questions.q: A student wants to write about collective social responsibility for their post-1914 essay. Which text and character best support this theme?
questions.explain: Inspector Goole's message that 'we are members of one body' directly dramatises collective social responsibility.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE English Literature (1ET0) specification; Paper 1: Shakespeare and Post-1914 Literature
